c.tagline: High-altitude gateway to Lake Titicaca's floating reed islands and Andean traditions.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are unmetered; agree on the fare before getting in, typically S/5-10 for short trips within town.

emergency.note: Response times can be slow and resources limited; for serious issues, private clinics or evacuation to Cusco/Arequipa/Lima is often recommended. Altitude sickness (soroche) is a common concern at 3,830m.

avoid.reason: Caution at night around the centre

hood_desc: The historic civic center of Puno, anchored by the Puno Cathedral and surrounding colonial-era buildings, restaurants and travel agencies.
The lakeside port area where boats depart for the Uros floating islands, Taquile and Amantani; lined with waterfront restaurants and the striking Yavari steamship museum.
A hillside barrio above downtown topped by a small park with panoramic views over the city and Lake Titicaca, known for its steep stairways and modest homes.
Puno's main pedestrian shopping street, packed with alpaca-wool shops, cafes and artisan stalls connecting the plaza to the market area.
A quieter, more residential district on the edge of downtown popular with mid-range hotels seeking a calmer base away from the tourist crush.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water only; altitude also makes hydration important.

transit.pay: Cash only, paid directly to the driver
transit.map: No official app; routes are learned locally or via hotel staff
transit.note: Public transit is informal and combis can be crowded; most visitors use taxis, mototaxis, or join organized boat tours to reach the port and islands.

air: Inca Manco Capac International Airport (JUL) in nearby Juliaca
train: PeruRail tourist train connecting Puno and Cusco
bus: Frequent long-distance buses to Cusco, Arequipa and La Paz, Bolivia
ferry: Boats to the Uros floating islands, Taquile and Amantani on Lake Titicaca

tip.r: Not obligatory, but a 10% tip is appreciated in tourist restaurants; tour guides and boat crews for Titicaca excursions are commonly tipped a few soles per person.

food.name: Trucha del Titicaca
food.desc: Rainbow trout farmed in Lake Titicaca, served fried whole, grilled a la plancha or in ceviche, with golden potatoes and habas.

places.name: Mojsa Restaurant
places.note: Long-running upstairs favourite on the main square; trout done grilled, in butter sauce or as ceviche.

places.name: Balcones de Puno
places.note: Trout and alpaca plates with nightly Altiplano music and dance; a Puno institution.

places.name: Mercado Central de Puno
places.note: Lunchtime stalls fry fresh trout and serve ceviche de trucha at local prices.

food.name: Chairo puneno
food.desc: Thick Altiplano broth of lamb and beef, chuno (freeze-dried potato), habas and wheat; the classic high-altitude warmer.

places.name: Mercado Central de Puno
places.note: Morning caldo stalls ladle out chairo the way puneno families make it.

places.name: Restaurante Tulipans
places.note: Casual courtyard spot on the pedestrian street with regional soups on the daily menu.

places.name: La Casona Restaurant
places.note: One of Puno's oldest dining rooms, strong on traditional Altiplano soups and stews.

food.name: Sopa y pesque de quinua
food.desc: Quinoa from the Altiplano as a creamy soup or as pesque, quinoa whipped with milk and cheese, eaten as a side or breakfast.

places.name: Mojsa Restaurant
places.note: Andean menu with quinoa soups and quinoa-crusted mains alongside the trout.

places.name: Colors Restaurant
places.note: Reliable central kitchen doing quinoa soup and Novo Andino plates for travellers.

places.name: Mercado Bellavista
places.note: Neighbourhood market where quinoa soups and pesque are everyday breakfast food.

food.name: Cancacho ayavireno
food.desc: Lamb or suckling pig marinated in aji panca and chicha then slow-roasted in a wood oven, a Sunday specialty of the Puno region.

places.name: Balcones de Puno
places.note: Regional roast meats plus folk music make it the easiest place in town to try cancacho.

places.name: Mercado Central de Puno
places.note: Weekend stalls sell wood-oven roast lamb by the plate with potatoes and salsa criolla.

places.name: La Casona Restaurant
places.note: Traditional Puno dining room that keeps regional roasts on the menu year-round.

food.name: Alpaca a la parrilla
food.desc: Lean, iron-rich alpaca steak grilled and served with Andean potatoes, quinoa or a huacatay sauce; a staple of Puno's Novo Andino menus.

places.name: IncaBar
places.note: Buzzy central bar-restaurant known for alpaca steaks and craft Peruvian beers.

places.name: Mojsa Restaurant
places.note: Alpaca and trout done well with a view over the cathedral square.

places.name: Colors Restaurant
places.note: Popular travellers' spot with grilled alpaca and Andean sides.

food.name: Thimpo de karachi
food.desc: Soupy stew of karachi, a small native Titicaca fish, simmered with potatoes, chuno and aji; deeply local lakeside eating.

places.name: Mercado Central de Puno
places.note: Fish counters and adjoining caldo stalls serve thimpo and karachi frito at midday.

places.name: Puerto de Puno food stalls
places.note: Cheap lakeside cookshops near the boat pier specialising in lake fish.

places.name: Mercado Bellavista
places.note: Local market where Titicaca fish dishes are cooked to order for neighbourhood diners.

food.name: Mate de coca
food.desc: Hot infusion of coca leaves, drunk all day in Puno at 3,830m to ease soroche; often blended with muna mint or chamomile.

places.name: Casa del Corregidor
places.note: Colonial-house cafe pouring coca and muna infusions plus highland coffee.

places.name: Ricos Pan
places.note: Beloved local bakery-cafe for breakfast mate de coca with fresh bread and pastries.

places.name: Mercado Central de Puno
places.note: Herb vendors sell coca leaves and brew mate by the glass for a few soles.

food.name: Api de quinua y maiz morado
food.desc: Thick, sweet hot drink of purple corn and quinoa spiced with cinnamon and clove, the Altiplano breakfast staple served with bunuelos.

places.name: Mercado Central de Puno
places.note: Early-morning api stalls pour it steaming alongside fried bunuelos.

places.name: Mercado Bellavista
places.note: Neighbourhood market where vendors ladle api into glasses from dawn.

places.name: Ricos Pan
places.note: Sit-down bakery option for warm Andean breakfast drinks in the centre.

landmarks: Uros Floating Islands
Astonishing man-made islands of woven totora reed on Lake Titicaca, where Uros families maintain a centuries-old way of life afloat.
Taquile Island
A UNESCO-recognised island whose men famously knit their own textiles, offering terraced hikes and shimmering lake vistas at 3,950 metres.
Amantaní Island
A tranquil island of stone paths and hilltop temples to Pachatata and Pachamama, beloved for homestays and star-filled Titicaca nights.
Sillustani
An eerie pre-Inca necropolis of towering cylindrical chullpa burial towers set on a peninsula above the glassy Lake Umayo.
Catedral Basílica San Carlos Borromeo
Puno's 18th-century Andean-Baroque cathedral, its intricately carved stone facade blending Spanish design with indigenous symbols on the Plaza de Armas.
Plaza de Armas and Casa del Corregidor
The city's colonial heart, framed by the cathedral and a 17th-century balconied house now hosting a cultural café.
Mirador Kuntur Wasi
A giant condor sculpture atop a steep stairway climb, spreading its wings over the finest panorama of Puno and Lake Titicaca.
Cerrito de Huajsapata
A rocky hill crowned by a monument to Manco Cápac, the legendary founder of the Inca Empire said to have risen from Titicaca.
Yavarí Steamship
An 1862 iron gunboat carried up the Andes in pieces by mule, lovingly restored as a museum ship moored on Titicaca's shore.
Arco Deustua
A 19th-century stone triumphal arch built by the townspeople to honour patriots fallen in Peru's independence battles of Junín and Ayacucho.

train.note: No international trains. PeruRail's Titicaca train runs the daytime route between Puno and Cusco a few times a week over the 4,300 m La Raya pass, taking about 10 hours - slower and far dearer than the bus but one of the most scenic rides in the Andes. The Belmond Andean Explorer sleeper also calls here. Book on the PeruRail site well ahead in the June-August season.

intl.to: Copacabana & La Paz (Bolivia) - via the Kasani border, ~3 hr to Copacabana

intl.op: Trans Titicaca / Panamericano — tickets at the Puno terminal

bus.note: Puno is the standard crossing point into Bolivia. The Copacabana route via Kasani is the prettier one, hugging the lake; Desaguadero is faster but grim. Hop buses have staff who walk you through the stamps, which is why travellers pay a premium over the local carriers. Domestic coaches from the Terminal Terrestre reach Cusco in about 7 hours and Arequipa in 6 on Cruz del Sur (https://www.cruzdelsur.com.pe/) and Civa.

intl.to: Uros floating islands, Taquile & Amantaní (Peru) - from the Puno muelle, 30 min to 3 hr
intl.op: local boat association operators — tickets at the port or through agencies

ferry.note: There is no scheduled international sailing across Lake Titicaca - the Bolivian side is reached by road. The launches from Puno's pier to the Uros reed islands and on to Taquile and Amantaní run daily and are the reason most people come, sold as half- or full-day trips or as overnight homestays. The lake sits at 3,800 m, so take the altitude seriously before a long boat day.

half.name: Chucuito
half.blurb: Colonial town about 20 minutes south holds the Inca Uyo, a walled complex of carved stone structures once linked to fertility rites.

half.name: Juli
half.blurb: Colonial town about 90 minutes away is known as 'Little Rome' for four large 16th-century churches built during Spanish evangelization.

half.name: Pucará
half.blurb: Pre-Inca ceremonial site about 90 minutes away is known for carved stone monoliths and the toritos de Pucará ceramic bulls made there.

half.name: Lampa
half.blurb: Pink-hued colonial town about 90 minutes away holds a replica of St. Peter's Basilica dome and catacombs beneath its main church.
